channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan adopt joint statement following talks in Astana
item.description: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan have adopted a joint statement outlining cooperation priorities after talks between Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Emomali Rahmon in Astana. Discussions covered railway transport, water resource management, trade, energy, agriculture, industry, and digitalization. Bilateral trade exceeded $1 billion in the first nine months of the year.

item.title: Uzbekistan exported $1.3 billion in fruits and vegetables in 9 months
item.description: Uzbekistan exported over $1.3 billion worth of fruits and vegetables in the first nine months of the year, with vegetables constituting the largest share. More than 1.5 million tons of produce were delivered abroad during this period.

item.title: Central Asian Trade Facilitation Meeting to be Held in Bishkek
item.description: A regional meeting of national trade facilitation committees from Central Asian countries will take place in Bishkek on November 9-10. Participants will discuss eliminating trade barriers, customs digitalization, and logistics development. The event aims to simplify trade and transit within the region and explore export opportunities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Advances Digital Development with New Strategies and Increased Internet Penetration
item.description: Uzbekistan has shifted digitalization from isolated projects to a core state policy, transforming governance, exports, and investment. The 'Digital Uzbekistan-2030' strategy, AI strategy, and Cybersecurity Strategy are key initiatives. Internet penetration reaches 94.2%, with 16.8 million users accessing 905 interactive government services. The country rose to 63rd in the UN e-government ranking.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Sign Joint Statement to Enhance Cooperation
item.description: Following talks, the leaders of Kazakhstan and Tajikistan signed a Joint Statement outlining priority areas for further cooperation. The document details the development of bilateral relations and key tasks for future interaction. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon, visiting Astana, was awarded the Qoja Ahmet Yasaui Order by Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

item.title: Ukraine Launches Major Drone Attack on Russia, Causing Fires at Oil Plant and Military Facility
item.description: Ukraine conducted a significant drone attack on Russia, resulting in fires at an oil plant in Saratov and a military facility in Oryol. Oryol Governor Andrey Klichkov confirmed an attack on an enterprise in the city's Sovetsky district but did not disclose the specific plant targeted.

item.title: US Strikes Iranian Air Defense Site Near Qeshm Island Amid Tensions
item.description: The U.S. military struck an air defense installation near Iran's southern Qeshm Island, confirmed by U.S. President Donald Trump. He stated the strike quickly disabled the facility. This incident occurs amid heightened tensions between the U.S. and Iran in the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Belgium Adopts Controversial Law Allowing Detention of Undocumented Migrants
item.description: Belgium has passed a contentious law enabling police to detain undocumented migrants in their homes, previously only possible in public spaces. The law targets individuals deemed a 'danger to public order or national security.' Critics warn of potential abuses due to vague wording. Protests have occurred nationwide against the new measures.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reviews Development of Tokmok City and Regions
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov visited Tokmok city and the Chuy and Kemin regions to review their socio-economic development plans for 2021-2026. He assessed implemented and future investment projects, infrastructure development, and regional issues. The city has seen growth in its production sector with new enterprises creating jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Public Debt Nears $10.4 Billion, New Tourism Project Launched
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's state debt reached 907 billion soms ($10.37 billion) as of September 30, with external and internal obligations nearly equal. The 'Ala-Too Resort' mountain cluster project, costing €1.2 billion, plans to open its first phase on December 1, aiming to attract 2 million tourists annually.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev awards Tajik President Rahmon the Order of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has awarded Tajik President Emomali Rahmon the Order of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi. Tokayev highlighted the deep symbolic meaning of the ceremony, emphasizing the centuries-old friendship and spiritual unity between the Kazakh and Tajik peoples. He noted Yasawi's legacy as a significant figure of the Islamic Renaissance.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Opposition Unites to Nominate Single Presidential Candidate
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's United Democratic Movement plans to select a single candidate for the presidential elections scheduled for January 27, 2027. Four contenders are currently being considered. The movement aims to consolidate opposition forces and engage civil society, advocating for free elections, human rights, and the rule of law.

item.title: Taliban Interior Minister's Bodyguard Found Dead in Baghlan Province
item.description: Local sources in Baghlan province reported the discovery of the body of a personal bodyguard to Taliban Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani. The bodyguard, identified as Qari Noor Jan Ahmadzai, also known as "Tayeb Badri," was found shot dead on Friday in the Dand Ghori district. This incident occurs despite Taliban claims of ensuring nationwide security.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Customs Seizes Psychotropic Drugs Smuggled from Kazakhstan
item.description: Kyrgyz customs officials have uncovered a channel for the illegal import and sale of psychotropic substances from Kazakhstan into Bishkek. The drugs were distributed through major pharmacy chains in the capital. Two individuals have been detained and charged with illegal drug manufacturing and trafficking, with an ongoing investigation to identify further participants in the scheme.

item.title: Uzbekistan Gas Consumption Varies Significantly Between Summer and Winter
item.description: Analysis of gas consumption data from 3.8 million meters in Uzbekistan reveals a stark difference between summer and winter usage. Average monthly consumption in private homes was 20 cubic meters in July and 500 cubic meters in January, a 25-fold increase. Tashkent recorded the highest average gas consumption per household, despite smaller average house sizes.

item.title: Almaty Develops Civil Sector to Address Key Urban Social Issues
item.description: Almaty is fostering its civil sector, with over 5,000 registered NGOs, to tackle important social problems. Approximately 30% focus on social protection, 25% on youth and education, and others on ecology, legal aid, culture, and sports. The city administration supports NGOs through funding and free consultations, and involves them in urban planning and policy discussions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Consistently Ranks Among Tajikistan's Top Three Trade Partners
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev noted that Kazakhstan is consistently among Tajikistan's top three trade partners. He praised the positive dynamics in Kazakh-Tajik relations, highlighting increased trade volume and diversification of goods. Bilateral trade regularly exceeds $1 billion annually, fostering robust business ties and cultural exchanges.

item.title: Kazakh President Awards Tajik Counterpart Order of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev presented Tajik President Emomali Rahmon with the Order of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi. Tokayev highlighted the deep historical and spiritual ties between the Kazakh and Tajik peoples, emphasizing their shared heritage from prominent thinkers like Khoja Ahmed Yasawi. He noted that Yasawi's teachings promote morality, justice, and humanism, uniting people for centuries.

item.title: Ulytau Region Discusses Prospects for Small and Medium Business Development
item.description: The governor of Ulytau region, Yeset Baiken, discussed prospects for small and medium business development with local entrepreneurs. He noted that over 16,000 SMEs operate in the region, emphasizing the need to create real conditions for production and sales, beyond just credit and subsidies, as per the President's directive. The meeting aimed to foster a favorable business environment and attract investment.

item.title: Kazakh and Tajik Presidents Hold Meeting in Astana, Emphasize Strategic Partnership
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev welcomed Tajik President Emomali Rahmon to Astana for an official visit. The leaders held talks, with Tokayev noting the strong strategic partnership and allied relations between the two nations. He expressed respect for the Tajik people and praised Tajikistan's significant reforms and achievements under Rahmon's leadership. Both sides aim to advance bilateral cooperation and implement mutually beneficial projects.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Demands Thorough Investigation into Suspicious Death
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered a renewed investigation into the death of Nurlan Almashev, whose mother disputes the initial finding of accidental choking. She claims evidence of bruises and blood on his clothing, and alleges procedural violations. The President has deemed the circumstances suspicious and requested the prosecutor's office to oversee the review, ensuring all of the mother's concerns are addressed.

item.title: Kyrgyz Citizens in Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg Advised to Enhance Security Measures
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Embassy in Belgium has urged citizens in Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg to enhance security measures amid widespread protests in several European countries. Diplomats recommend avoiding crowded places and being aware of potential transport restrictions. Citizens are advised to follow local authorities' instructions and monitor official sources.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kurultai Fully Supports President Tokayev's Initiatives in Address
item.description: The Kurultai of Kazakhstan has announced its full support for the initiatives presented in President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address to the nation. The address, titled 'Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Period,' is seen as opening a new, high-quality phase in the country's history and outlining its development path for decades to come.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Holds Talks with Tajik President Rahmon in Akorda
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held talks with Tajik President Emomali Rahmon at the Akorda presidential palace. The meeting focused on bilateral cooperation and regional issues between the two Central Asian nations.

item.title: Muratbek Azimbakiev Officially Assumes Role as Kyrgyzstan's WTO Representative
item.description: Muratbek Azimbakiev has officially taken up his duties as Kyrgyzstan's Permanent Representative to the WTO. He presented his credentials to the WTO Director-General, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. Discussions focused on trade facilitation, digitalization, and market access for Kyrgyz goods, as well as support for landlocked developing countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan-Tajikistan Trade Surges 26% as Presidents Discuss Cooperation
item.description: Presidents Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Emomali Rahmon held talks in Astana, discussing expanded trade and cooperation in transport, energy, and agriculture. Bilateral trade exceeded $1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, a 26% increase year-on-year. Kazakhstan is among Tajikistan's top three trade partners.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan Discuss New Joint Projects as Trade Exceeds One Billion Dollars
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon to discuss new joint projects. Trade between the two nations has surpassed one billion dollars, with over 130 Kazakh-invested enterprises operating in Tajikistan. Both leaders emphasized the strong strategic partnership and friendly relations between their countries.

item.title: Four Arrested in Kyrgyzstan for Illegally Transferring Over 11.5 Million Som from E-Wallets
item.description: Four individuals have been arrested in Bishkek in connection with the illegal transfer of over 11.5 million Kyrgyz som from electronic wallets. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that the funds were moved through numerous electronic transactions. A criminal case has been initiated, and investigations are ongoing to identify all accomplices.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Restrict Methane Gas Station Operations During Cold Weather
item.description: Uzbekistan may impose restrictions on the operation of methane gas stations during cold weather periods. Any such limitations will be implemented based on schedules agreed upon with local authorities. Consumers will be notified in advance of any necessary restrictions.

item.title: Taliban Report 437 People Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 99 families, totaling 437 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan on Saturday. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that returnees arrived through various border crossings, including Torkham, Spin Boldak in Kandahar, Silk Bridge in Nimroz, and Islam Qala in Herat.

item.title: Central Asian Regional Contact Group on Afghanistan Holds Second Meeting in Bishkek
item.description: The second meeting of the Regional Contact Group of Central Asian Special Representatives on Afghanistan convened in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Discussions focused on strengthening regional coordination for peace and security in Afghanistan, expanding economic and humanitarian cooperation, and improving regional connectivity.

item.title: Aktobe City Administration Cancels Rally for Social Rights of People with Disabilities
item.description: The Aktobe city administration has revoked its decision to permit a rally advocating for the social rights of people with disabilities, originally scheduled for December 3. The cancellation cites emergency repair works by 'Aqtobe su-energy group' as the reason. The administration could not offer an alternative date or location due to pre-planned events.

item.title: Tajikistan's New Migration Law Supports Those Displaced by Environmental Disasters
item.description: Tajikistan's new law on migration offers support to individuals relocated from hazardous areas. This includes land plots, financial aid, preferential loans, and free relocation. The law defines environmental migration as internal displacement due to environmental degradation or disasters, with specific government decrees detailing the process and aid.

item.title: Kazakhstan Among Tajikistan's Top Three Trade Partners, Bilateral Trade Exceeds $1 Billion
item.description: Kazakhstan has become one of Tajikistan's top three trading partners, with bilateral trade surpassing $1 billion in the first nine months of 2026, a nearly 26% increase year-on-year. Presidents of both nations noted the expansion of goods nomenclature and increased cargo transportation, alongside growing business contacts and investment cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh and Tajik Presidents Hold Talks, Emphasizing Strategic Partnership
item.description: The Presidents of Kazakhstan and Tajikistan held talks, with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighting the strategic partnership and alliance between the two nations. He praised Tajikistan's development successes under President Emomali Rahmon's leadership and noted the positive dynamics in bilateral relations across all areas.

item.title: Kazakh Farmers Raise Prices on Produce, Livestock, and Grains
item.description: Kazakh farmers have increased prices across various agricultural products. In January-October 2026, agricultural goods rose by 11.7%. Corn prices surged 13.9%, while fruits like grapes and cherries saw significant increases. Poultry and beef prices also climbed substantially.

item.title: UN Warns Afghanistan Faces Worsening Humanitarian Crisis Amid Rights Restrictions
item.description: The UN warns Afghanistan is facing a worsening humanitarian crisis five years after the Taliban's return, citing severe restrictions on women's and girls' rights, a fragile economy, and reduced aid. The UN official highlighted the critical educational challenges and the impact of returning migrants.

item.title: Four arrested in Bishkek for illegally transferring 11.5 million soms via e-wallet
item.description: Bishkek police have arrested four individuals in connection with the illegal transfer of over 11.5 million soms using an electronic wallet. Preliminary investigations by the Ministry of Internal Affairs suggest the funds were moved through numerous electronic transactions. Criminal proceedings have been initiated as authorities investigate the circumstances and roles of the detainees.

item.title: Company head and technologist jailed in Fergana poisoning case involving 105 children
item.description: A court of cassation overturned a previous sentence of restricted freedom, sentencing the head of a company to 4 years and the technologist to 3 years and 6 months in prison. This follows an incident where 105 children were poisoned. The initial ruling had imposed sentences of restricted freedom on the two individuals.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Welcomes Tajik President Rahmon for Official Visit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev officially welcomed Tajik President Emomali Rahmon in Astana. The visit included a welcoming ceremony with a demonstration flight and a meeting between the leaders and their delegations. Rahmon also attended a summit on AI security.
